problem: Goal-directed city navigation without step-by-step instructions (only landmark-relative goal descriptions and street views) is not solved by prior work: VLN methods need instructions and RL methods are sample-inefficient. A plain ReAct LLM agent is short-sighted and memoryless, so it loops and hits dead ends.
motivation: Long-range urban navigation needs self-localization and a spatial representation (cognitive map), yet landmarks are often invisible from a given street view. The paper observes that ReAct-style reaction fails in complex road networks, and draws on human cognition (memory and planning) to give LLM agents a memory-based cognitive map and long-term plans.
key_idea: A Perceive-Reflect-Plan (PReP) workflow: a fine-tuned LLaVA estimates landmark direction and distance, an episodic/semantic/working memory reflects on past trajectory and inferences to estimate goal direction, and an LLM planner decomposes the route into sub-goals.
insight: Reflection (memory) matters more than planning: removing reflection drops Beijing SR from 66 to 47, whereas removing planning drops it to 56. Fine-tuned perception is nearly as good as oracle GPS perception (about 4% SR lower). Success depends heavily on landmark visibility along the route, so the memory-based anticipation is what bridges the gaps. Distilling GPT-4-turbo trajectories into LLaMA3-8B helps (roughly 13% SR over base) but still leaves a large gap to GPT-4-turbo.
method: Perception: LLaVA-1.5-7B fine-tuned with LoRA on ~30k Q&A turns (landmark visible? -> bounding box -> distance) from about 8,000 images of 32 landmarks; outputs direction and distance of landmarks to the agent.
Goal direction inference: an LLM (optionally with a calculator) combines landmark positions and the goal description (cosine-theorem geometry) to infer the goal direction and distance R_gt.
Episodic memory: natural-language log of each step (position, options, action, arrival, and goal inference), used to retrieve past inferences and visited status of connected nodes.
Semantic memory: an LLM summarizes episodic memory into high-level lessons (e.g. detours), forming an intrinsic topological map.
Working memory (anticipate-reevaluate): when no landmark is visible, it anticipates the goal direction from past inferences and movement; when one is visible, it reevaluates and synthesizes R_lt.

Planning: long-term planner updates the previous plan into sub-goals (e.g. 'move east until an intersection') from reflected inference, memory and old plan; a short-term decision module picks the next road-connection action.

setting.backbone: Fine-tuned LLaVA-1.5-7B (perception) + GPT-4-turbo (frozen, reflection/planning); LLaMA3-8B fine-tuned variant
setting.training_data: LLaVA: ~30k Q&A turns from ~8,000 landmark images (32 landmarks, LoRA); LLaMA3-8B: ~20k dialogue turns per city from successful GPT-4-turbo trajectories in other cities; GPT-4-turbo is used with few-shot prompts
setting.observation: Street-view RGB images (90° FOV, 1024x512) at each road node, one per edge, plus road connectivity and textual goal description relative to landmarks
setting.action_space: Discrete moves along road-network nodes (50 m per step) in compass directions
setting.simulator: Custom graph-based urban environment built from Baidu/Google Street View and OpenStreetMap (Beijing, Shanghai, New York, Paris)
setting.privileged: None at test time (GT GPS distances used only in an oracle ablation); goal description given relative to landmarks

numbers.eval_set_note: 100 navigation tasks per city test set
numbers.extra: iteration limit 2.5x the minimum steps; text says 66.68% SR while table says 66

numbers.backbone: LLaMA3-8B fine-tuned on GPT-4-turbo trajectories + fine-tuned LLaVA
numbers.extra: fine-tuned on trajectories from another city

numbers_note: Custom benchmark of four cities, 100 tasks each; no standard benchmark. The Beijing SR is inconsistently reported (66.68% in text vs 66 in Table 1). Averages of SR across four cities ~54%.
results: PReP achieves SR of 66/51/47/49 (Beijing/Shanghai/New York/Paris), beating the strongest baselines such as DEPS (45/28/17/24) and CaP (47/23/12/17), and far above RL (13/13/8/10). Ablations show that removing reflection or planning reduces SR notably, and fine-tuned LLaVA is close to oracle perception.
limitations: Relies on closed-source GPT-4-turbo; fine-tuned LLaMA3-8B reaches far lower SR (e.g. 45 vs 66 in Beijing)
Small test sets (100 tasks per city) cause fluctuation; only 6-10 landmarks per city, 4 CBD areas, and simulation on a discretized street graph
Slow inference (~12 s per step) and success strongly depends on landmark visibility
